scenes.headline: NumPy Essentials
scenes.subtitle: Fast, vectorized numeric arrays
scenes.narration: NumPy powers the entire Python data stack with fast, memory-efficient N-dimensional arrays, and pandas itself is built directly on top of it.

scenes.headline: Python list vs ndarray
scenes.narration: A Python list can hold mixed types, but it stores a pointer to each object scattered across memory, which makes numeric loops slow. A NumPy ndarray instead holds a single dtype packed into one contiguous block of memory, so operations run as tight compiled C loops over that buffer. For numeric work at scale, that difference translates into speedups of one to two orders of magnitude.

scenes.headline: Vectorized operations
scenes.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
print(a * 2)          # [2 4 6 8]
print(a[a > 2])       # [3 4]
print(a.mean(), a.sum())
scenes.narration: Multiplying the array by two applies the operation element-wise across every value at once, with no Python loop in sight. Boolean indexing with a comparison lets you filter to just the elements that satisfy a condition. And reductions like mean and sum collapse the whole array into a single number, all executed in fast native code.

scenes.headline: Key concepts
scenes.narration: The dtype determines both how much memory each element uses and how much numeric precision you get, so choosing it deliberately matters. The shape describes an array's dimensions, and reshape rearranges those dimensions without copying data. Broadcasting lets arrays of compatible but different shapes combine seamlessly. And the axis argument tells reductions which direction to collapse, rows or columns.

scenes.headline: Broadcasting
scenes.code:
matrix = np.ones((3, 4))
row = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
result = matrix + row   # row added to every matrix row
scenes.narration: Here a one-dimensional row of length four is added to a three-by-four matrix. Broadcasting virtually stretches that smaller row across every row of the matrix, aligning their shapes, and adds it without ever physically copying the data. This is what makes many NumPy expressions both concise and remarkably efficient.

scenes.text: Vectorize with array operations instead of Python loops; NumPy is the foundation under pandas.
scenes.narration: Whenever you feel the urge to loop over numbers in Python, reach for a vectorized NumPy operation instead and let the compiled core do the heavy lifting.
